subject: Finlytics performance constraints & token surface plan
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@finlytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Finlytics performance constraints & token surface plan

Ellen —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap from our side and a proposed next-step plan so we can size a realistic SLO & deployment for your use case. I pulled the notes into three buckets: latency/throughput targets, context/token surface, and operational hedges.

1) Targets you called out on the call
- Latency: p95 < 250–300 ms for user-facing generation (interactive).
- Throughput: baseline 150–200 concurrent RPS, with burst to 350 RPS for short windows.
- Concurrency: expect ~50 long-lived concurrent chat sessions; spikes to ~200 during close-of-day reports.
- Streaming: partial output streaming required for the chat UI (we should start streaming token-by-token to the client).

2) Context & token surface (what you said)
- Typical prompt: 6–8k tokens of structured context (user profile + recent transactions) + ~1k expected model output.
- Peak sessions: up to 32k tokens (full ledger + long history) for investigative flows but those are <5% of total calls.

3) Immediate implications we flagged
- 32k contexts materially increase per-token latency — model exec and KV cache warm costs. For p95 <300ms we need either heavy prefix caching + summarization, or to route peaks to a higher-latency tier.
- Streaming helps perceived latency but does not remove the initial KV cache/setup cost for large contexts.
- Concurrency/throughput needs push toward Dedicated capacity or a reserved pool with burst.

Attachments: sending a sample prompt set and an initial SLO proposal (attached). Also a quick cost/latency spreadsheet will follow from Marcus.

Proposed next steps (quick wins):
- You share 10 representative prompts (redacted) + 1 week of anonymized request-size histogram — we can run a profiling pass and return realistic p50/p95 token latency numbers.
- Schedule a technical runbook + canary plan with our infra/ops: 60m session to map traffic shaping, KV cache TTLs, and fallback policy.
- We will propose a two-tier routing policy: interactive (p95 target) on Dedicated pool + bulk investigative requests route to a cost-optimized model variant with async processing.

Would you be able to drop the sample prompts and a short histogram to procurement@finlytics.com (cc'd) or directly to me? Happy to schedule the runbook — I have availability Thu 07/01 10:00–12:00 PT and Fri 07/02 14:00–16:00 PT.

Thanks,
Priyom

- Streaming: we definitely want token streaming in the UI for faster perceived response, but for investigative flows we can accept a longer tail. So streaming is required for "interactive" routes, optional for bulk investigative jobs.
- Fallbacks: if Dedicated capacity is exhausted, what's the best practice? Route to a smaller model variant (fewer tokens) or to an async queue? What's your recommended SLA for those fallbacks?

We will attach 12 redacted prompts and a representative histogram to the email thread by EOD today. Also looping in our ops lead (ops-eng-team).

Ellen — thanks for the quick reply and for sending the prompts. A couple of technical notes based on the scenarios you described: 

- 32k contexts: expect a ~3–5x increase in model execution time vs 8k, depending on model family and attention kernels. That means p95 will likely slip beyond interactive targets unless we apply either (a) summarization windowing at the client side, (b) aggressive KV/prefix caching on warm paths, or (c) model sharding that pins long-history sessions to Dedicated nodes.
- Streaming: helpful for perceived latency. For interactive routes we recommend enabling streaming with early token emission after the first 128–256 tokens are generated; that reduces perceived wait but does not eliminate initial KV costs.
- Fallback strategy: our recommended flow is: 1) allow routing to a smaller model variant (quantized) for degraded capacity with explicit token limits (max_output 512), 2) if request size > 16k tokens route to async job with progress notifications, 3) apply rate-limited admission control per-customer to protect SLO.
- Concurrency/Throughput: to reliably hit p95 <300ms at 150–200 RPS with an 8k context we advise a Dedicated pool sized with 6–8 accelerated GPU instances (depending on chosen model). For your burst profile we suggest a reserved burst bucket + autoscale policy.

I've attached a preliminary latency estimate workbook (Marcus prepared the numbers) and an internal checklist we use for canarying high-context workloads. Marcus — can you confirm the GPU spec assumptions (fp16 vs int8 quant) used in the sheet?

Action items
- Finlytics: upload 10–12 representative prompts + histogram (EOD).
- Redwood: run profiling pass on incoming artifacts and return p50/p95 curves + suggested Dedicated sizing and cost delta. (Target delivery by 07/05.)
- Schedule 60m runbook: proposed Thu 07/01 10:00 PT.

Ellen — appreciate the quick turnaround. Confirming the plan and next steps: 

1) You (Finlytics) will upload the redacted prompt set + a simple histogram of request sizes.
2) Marcus will run a profiling pass (we'll exercise 3 model stacks: base open model, quantized int8 variant, and a lower-capacity faster variant) and return a table of p50/p95 token latencies across 1k/8k/32k contexts. Marcus — can you aim to share the latency_estimates.xlsx by COB tomorrow?
3) We'll draft a runbook for the canary that includes: KV cache TTLs, admission control thresholds, model fallback policy, and a versioned rollback plan.
4) Tentatively schedule the runbook session Thu 07/01 10:00 PT. If that works for Finlytics ops, I'll send a calendar invite with a short agenda.

Notes on economics: routing large-context investigative flows async will cut cost ~40–60% vs keeping everything hot on Dedicated; we'll capture a cost delta in the spreadsheet. We recommend a short canary (48–72 hrs) with 10–20% traffic routed to Dedicated and the rest to a mixed pool to validate SLOs before committing reserved capacity.
